terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A one-piece moulding on four push-fit legs: nothing opens, turns or swings, and the umbrella hole is a hole rather than a socket -- the kit's umbrella is a separate floor-standing prop -- so one root pivot and zero sockets. Beer gardens and soi-side eateries set these out by the dozen, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. White plastic gone slightly cream, grey in the grooves where dust settles, scuffed at the feet; every beer garden and soi-side eatery, under a patio umbrella.

reasoning: TWO components on TWO materials: the TOP (one 64-segment closed lathe carrying skirt, flat ring, recessed field, raised disc and the hole wall -- a SOLID piece, nothing else merged in since v4) and the LEGS (four frusta and four foot pads merged). Two draw calls of two.

Two materials, both white polypropylene at 0.55 and both textureless as declared: the top carries the ribbing as ONE 1024 px canvas drawn in plan after construction (map + bump), the legs a faint 256 px grime canvas. They are two materials only because a plan-mapped picture of the top has nothing to say on a leg face.
No repetition system: the ribs are texture, not parts, and the whole prop sits at 1376 of 2000.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a big round shell top on four chunky square legs, read at prop distance by three things: the radial ribbing (a PBR map and bump map of 84 ridges on ONE solid lathe, since v4), the raised centre disc with a real hole through it, and the deep rim skirt. Without the ribs it is a plain cafe table; without the hole it is a lid.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.02 x 0.72 x 1.02 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 1.02 m disc with a 0.072 m skirt at 0.648-0.720, its top a 0.062 flat ring around a field recessed 6 mm carrying 84 radial ribs as a bump-mapped texture, a 0.30 m raised centre disc 2 mm proud with a 46 mm hole, on four square tapered legs 0.115 at the top to 0.092 at the foot on a 0.571 m square.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z +-0.510 at the rim, y 0 to 0.722 at the raised centre disc. The LIST-TIME declaration was 0.90 dia x 0.72 (w/h 1.25). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.899 x 1.332 x 1.901, w/h = d/h 1.426 with a round plan, and the plate agrees the table is squat: the top ellipse's minor/major of 0.54 puts the camera at 33 degrees, and the legs' 400 px against the 850 px top come to 0.56 D after the cos correction, so the plate itself reads w/h 1.4-1.55. Height is the axis a table keeps -- a monobloc dining table is 0.70-0.72 m and this one pairs with the stool and the umbrella -- so diameter = 0.72 x 1.426 = 1.027 -> 1.02 m, the 100 cm class, and the declaration was corrected before building. Stations off the proxy in fractions of H: top rows 0.88-0.98 with 0.94/0.96 hollow inside (a shell with a 0.10 H = 0.072 m rim skirt; the plate's rim is 60 of 850 px, the same 0.07 D); legs at columns 10-20 and 59-69 = 0.125 W wide on centres 0.3125 W out, the z range the same; BUILT at 0.28 W (a 0.571 m square) from v3, because at the proxy's 0.3125 W the legs' outer corners stood 22 mm outside the round top (owner review) -- the proxy fuses the leg with the skirt above it and over-reads the centre; leg columns straight from row 0.86 to 0.00, the plate adding a slight taper (110 px at the top, 95 at the foot).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.899 x 1.332 x 1.901, w/h 1.426, which with the plate's own 1.4-1.55 is what corrected the declared diameter from 0.90 to 1.02. Every station above is the proxy band table in fractions of H; the plate settled the leg taper and the ring/field/disc split, which the 20 mm proxy voxel fuses.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/ribs.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.850. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: Measured on the plate: ridges #eae7e7 / #f5f5f4 (232-245) with grooves #b0b0af (176) between them; rim skirt #f5f5f4; legs #e2ddd1 lit and #efe7d2 in shade, analyze_texture meanLum 236.8 sat 0.016 specularFraction 0.735; extract_pbr_evidence palette #EBE8E5 #D5D3CF #E1DFDB #C3C1BD #A8A6A2 at confidence 0.85.

Textureless as DECLARED: one tone 0xeeebe4 as a vertex colour on a solid lathe, and the ribbing as ONE 1024 px canvas drawn in plan AFTER construction (ribtop tile, planUV at the diameter) bound as map and bumpMap (bumpScale 0.02): 84 ridge crowns at 1.0, groove floors at 176/238 = 0.74 with rounded shoulders, rust-brown specks lying in the grooves, the disc cross-marks and the step hairlines. v4: the ribs were 80 boxes; the owner asked for a solid top with only a PBR texture.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: plastic (top, with the ribtop canvas) and plasticLeg (legs, with the grime canvas): 2 of 2.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1376 of 2000: a 64-segment lathe of 11 profile points, four frusta and four pads. v3 was 1904 with 80 rib boxes at 40 segments; v4 spends the difference on a rounder rim.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: One closed lathe for the shell, ring, field, disc and hole -- the ribs and cross marks are texture; frusta for the legs; boxes for the foot pads.
No InstancedMesh at two draw calls. In a scene the HOST instances the table.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. One 1024 px ribtop canvas (map + bump, 4 MB) on the top and one 256 px grime canvas on the legs, bound after construction; the factory built in 116 ms.

risks.description: The list-time 0.90 diameter disagreed with the proxy's 1.426 aspect by 14%.
risks.mitigation: Corrected to 1.02 on the height axis before building; arithmetic recorded on the asset notes and in envelopeDerivation.

risks.description: Ribs as a bump map have no silhouette: seen at a grazing angle the top is smooth.
risks.mitigation: Accepted by the owner (v4: a solid top with only a PBR texture); the 6 mm field recess and the 2 mm disc step stay in the lathe profile, so the top is not a flat plate.

risks.description: The umbrella hole is a real opening.
risks.mitigation: At 46 mm and the turntable's 20-degree elevation it does not show the backdrop; if the gate flags it the flag is honest and is covered with --allow-holes on a holeviz measurement.
